"""
A payload as it is written inside a document's string, which quotes the way a JSON string does.
"""
def graphql_escape_payload(payload):
  return payload.replace("\\", "\\\\").replace("\"", "\\\"")

"""
Whether the run was given a way to tell a true answer from a false one off the page itself.
"""
def boolean_oracle_given():
  return any((menu.options.string, menu.options.not_string, menu.options.regexp, menu.options.code))

"""
Whether the page says the injected condition held.

The answer a target gives where it branches on the command rather than printing what it returned -
the page it renders, or the status it answers with, stands in for the output a blind sink withholds.
"""
def boolean_oracle(page, code=None, page_length=None, headers=None):
  """
  Read against the headers as well as the body, the way the reference for this reads it: what tells
  a true answer from a false one is as often something the application set in a header - a cookie
  it drops, a location it redirects to, a length it reports - as anything it rendered, and a body
  read on its own never sees it. The pattern is matched the way that one matches it too, without
  regard to case and with '^' and '$' reading the lines of the answer rather than the whole of it.
  """
  answered = page or ""
  if headers:
    try:
      answered = "".join(str(line) for line in headers.headers) + answered
    except AttributeError:
      answered = str(headers) + answered
  if menu.options.string:
    return menu.options.string in answered
  if menu.options.not_string:
    return menu.options.not_string not in answered
  if menu.options.regexp:
    try:
      return bool(re.search(menu.options.regexp, answered, re.IGNORECASE | re.MULTILINE))
    except re.error:
      return None
  if menu.options.code is not None:
    return str(code) == str(menu.options.code)
  """
  '--lengths' asked for by name, or 'page_length' handed in because there was no body to read at
  all ('--null-connection') - either way, a length and nothing else is what there is to bisect on.
  """
  if menu.options.lengths or page_length is not None:
    if settings.BOOLEAN_TRUE_LENGTH is None or settings.BOOLEAN_FALSE_LENGTH is None:
      return None
    if page_length is None:
      page_length = len(page) if page is not None else None
    if page_length is None or settings.BOOLEAN_TRUE_LENGTH == settings.BOOLEAN_FALSE_LENGTH:
      return None
    to_true = abs(page_length - settings.BOOLEAN_TRUE_LENGTH)
    to_false = abs(page_length - settings.BOOLEAN_FALSE_LENGTH)
    if to_true == to_false:
      return None
    return to_true < to_false
  # Nothing was named, so the answer is read against the two pages a known question came back with:
  # whichever of them this response is closer to is the answer it carries. Calibrated rather than
  # compared to a threshold, because what a condition changes can be a couple of characters of a
  # page that is otherwise thousands - a difference no ratio of the whole would notice.
  if settings.BOOLEAN_TRUE_PAGE is None or settings.BOOLEAN_FALSE_PAGE is None or page is None:
    return None
  current = comparable_page(page)
  to_true = page_ratio(settings.BOOLEAN_TRUE_PAGE, current)
  to_false = page_ratio(settings.BOOLEAN_FALSE_PAGE, current)
  if to_true == to_false:
    return None
  return to_true > to_false

"""
Learn what a yes and a no look like on this target, from two questions whose answers are known.

False where the two are indistinguishable: a page that reads the same either way carries no answer,
and everything bisected on it would be noise.
"""
def calibrate_boolean_oracle(page_true, page_false, code_true=None, code_false=None):
  settings.BOOLEAN_TRUE_PAGE = settings.BOOLEAN_FALSE_PAGE = None
  settings.BOOLEAN_TRUE_RAW = settings.BOOLEAN_FALSE_RAW = None
  settings.BOOLEAN_TRUE_LENGTH = settings.BOOLEAN_FALSE_LENGTH = None
  settings.BOOLEAN_TRUE_CODE, settings.BOOLEAN_FALSE_CODE = code_true, code_false
  if page_true is None or page_false is None:
    return False
  # Worth paying a fresh connection per request for '--null-connection' only past a minimum size -
  # settled once, off the page this run actually has, rather than assumed.
  if settings.NULL_CONNECTION_WORTHWHILE is None:
    settings.NULL_CONNECTION_WORTHWHILE = len(page_true) >= settings.NULL_CONNECTION_MIN_LENGTH
  true_page, false_page = comparable_page(page_true), comparable_page(page_false)
  """
  Read as a length once the target's own moving parts are out of it.

  A length is a length whichever bytes it counts, so the pages themselves are measured as they came
  back - but whether that length says anything is another question. A target printing something of
  its own that varies in width, a timing or a counter, is a different number of bytes long on two
  identical requests, and a difference read off that is the page moving rather than the question
  being answered: taken for an answer, any boundary at all is confirmed on the strength of it.
  """
  true_length, false_length = len(page_true), len(page_false)
  lengths_distinguish = true_length != false_length and len(true_page) != len(false_page)
  if lengths_distinguish:
    settings.BOOLEAN_TRUE_LENGTH, settings.BOOLEAN_FALSE_LENGTH = true_length, false_length
  if not true_page or true_page == false_page:
    # Content alone cannot tell the two apart - length still might, and is reported precisely
    # because it is the only one of the two that just did.
    return lengths_distinguish
  """
  A page that is a plain shell error on both questions is not two answers - it is one error, with
  this run's own calibration digits echoed back inside it. A filter that corrupts the payload before
  a shell ever sees it still leaves the random marker's length (6 vs. 7) sitting in the "command not
  found" text the shell quotes it in, which tells the two pages apart without either command having
  actually run. Normalizing the digits out of each error catches exactly that case, without touching
  a real difference in wording a target's own interpreter would give for two different questions.
  """
  true_error, false_error = extract_error_message(page_true), extract_error_message(page_false)
  if true_error is not None and false_error is not None:
    normalized = lambda text: re.sub(r"\d+", "#", text)
    if normalized(true_error) == normalized(false_error):
      return False
  settings.BOOLEAN_TRUE_PAGE, settings.BOOLEAN_FALSE_PAGE = true_page, false_page
  settings.BOOLEAN_TRUE_RAW, settings.BOOLEAN_FALSE_RAW = page_true, page_false
  return True

"""
What a finding's oracle looked like when it was confirmed, kept under the finding's own key.

The calibration lives in settings, so whatever calibrates - or fails to - after it overwrites it, and
what is read later, at quit(), would then be read against another parameter's pages.
"""
def remember_oracle(key):
  settings.ORACLE_STATES[key] = (settings.BOOLEAN_TRUE_PAGE, settings.BOOLEAN_FALSE_PAGE,
                                 settings.BOOLEAN_TRUE_RAW, settings.BOOLEAN_FALSE_RAW,
                                 settings.BOOLEAN_TRUE_LENGTH, settings.BOOLEAN_FALSE_LENGTH,
                                 settings.BOOLEAN_TRUE_CODE, settings.BOOLEAN_FALSE_CODE,
                                 settings.BOOLEAN_PRINTED_STATE, list(settings.DYNAMIC_MARKINGS))

"""
Put a finding's own oracle back before anything is read through it - once per retrieval, from the
thread that starts it, so the workers it fans out to only ever read it.
"""
def restore_oracle(key):
  state = settings.ORACLE_STATES.get(key)
  if state is None:
    return
  settings.BOOLEAN_TRUE_PAGE, settings.BOOLEAN_FALSE_PAGE = state[0], state[1]
  settings.BOOLEAN_TRUE_RAW, settings.BOOLEAN_FALSE_RAW = state[2], state[3]
  settings.BOOLEAN_TRUE_LENGTH, settings.BOOLEAN_FALSE_LENGTH = state[4], state[5]
  settings.BOOLEAN_TRUE_CODE, settings.BOOLEAN_FALSE_CODE = state[6], state[7]
  settings.BOOLEAN_PRINTED_STATE = state[8]
  settings.DYNAMIC_MARKINGS = list(state[9])

"""
Text one answer carries and the other does not, quoted back as the option that would name it.

Worked out from the two pages a known question came back with, so that a finding made by calibration
can be reached again without it - the next run is told what a true answer looks like instead of
having to learn it. Where the two answers differ by a word that also appears elsewhere on the page,
the word alone would match either of them, so it is grown outwards into the text around it until it
is text only that answer carries: 'up' is on both pages, 'Host is up' on one.

Nothing is offered where the difference is not the target's to make: a payload that prints its own
marker is answered by a word this run invented, which would mean nothing to the next one.
"""
def inferred_boolean_oracle():
  if settings.BOOLEAN_PRINTED_STATE:
    return ""
  true_raw, false_raw = settings.BOOLEAN_TRUE_RAW, settings.BOOLEAN_FALSE_RAW
  if not true_raw or not false_raw:
    return ""

  # The shortest window around the difference that the other answer has no copy of.
  def unique_around(page, other, start, end):
    for margin in settings.BOOLEAN_STRING_HINT_MARGINS:
      low, high = max(0, start - margin), min(len(page), end + margin)
      # A window that opens inside a tag is snapped back to the start of it, so what is quoted does
      # not begin with half an element.
      reach = max(0, low - settings.BOOLEAN_STRING_HINT_MAXLEN)
      opened = page.rfind("<", reach, low)
      if opened > page.rfind(">", reach, low):
        low = opened
      head, tail = page[low:start], page[start:high]
      """
      The markup around a difference is often the difference.

      A scenario page that lists its own source carries both branches as text, so the words alone
      are on both answers and only the rendered one is wrapped in its tag. The window is therefore
      quoted as it stands first, and only cut back to the words inside it when that is not enough.
      """
      shapes = [head + tail]
      if ">" in head or "<" in tail:
        shapes.append((head.rsplit(">", 1)[1] if ">" in head else head) +
                      (tail.split("<", 1)[0] if "<" in tail else tail))
      for shape in shapes:
        candidate = shape.strip().split(settings.END_LINE.LF)[0].strip(" \"'\t\r")
        candidate = candidate[:settings.BOOLEAN_STRING_HINT_MAXLEN].strip()
        if len(candidate) < 2 or not candidate.isprintable():
          continue
        if candidate in other or candidate not in page:
          continue
        return candidate
    return ""

  # A status code that differs is the cheapest answer of all, and the one least likely to move.
  true_code, false_code = settings.BOOLEAN_TRUE_CODE, settings.BOOLEAN_FALSE_CODE
  if true_code and false_code and str(true_code) != str(false_code) and str(true_code) not in settings.WAF_BLOCK_HTTP_CODES:
    return "--code=" + str(true_code)

  # What the page shows, before anything with markup in it: a line of it reads as something a person
  # looking at the page would point at, and a single word of it survives a target that renders the
  # same answer a little differently.
  def lines(page):
    return set(filtered_page_content(page, split=settings.END_LINE.LF).split(settings.END_LINE.LF))

  def words(page):
    return set(filtered_page_content(page).split())

  """
  Where the two answers actually part company, as spans of each page.

  A page is not only its answer: a run that took a moment longer, a counter, a length printed in a
  corner will all differ between two requests without saying anything about what was asked. Text is
  only worth quoting when it sits where the answer changed, so a candidate has to overlap one of
  these to count - otherwise the page's own furniture can stand in for the answer and be offered as
  the way to recognise it.
  """
  opcodes = [_ for _ in difflib.SequenceMatcher(None, false_raw, true_raw).get_opcodes() if _[0] != "equal"]
  changed_true = [(j1, j2) for _, _, _, j1, j2 in opcodes]
  changed_false = [(i1, i2) for _, i1, i2, _, _ in opcodes]

  def overlaps_change(candidate, page, regions):
    at = page.find(candidate)
    while at != -1:
      if any(at < high and low < at + len(candidate) for low, high in regions):
        return True
      at = page.find(candidate, at + 1)
    return False

  """
  The page's own moving parts are not an answer either.

  Sitting where the two answers differ is not enough on its own: a target that prints something of
  its own that moves - a timing, a counter, a clock - differs there between two identical requests
  as well, so that text lands in the difference without having anything to do with what was asked.
  Those regions were measured from two samples of the same request before any of this, and taken
  out of the comparison every other reading is made through; read through it here too, text that is
  only the page moving is gone, and what is offered is what the answer actually changed.
  """
  true_steady, false_steady = remove_dynamic_content(true_raw), remove_dynamic_content(false_raw)

  def usable(candidate, page, other, regions, steady):
    candidate = candidate.strip()
    return (candidate and candidate in page and candidate not in other
            and overlaps_change(candidate, page, regions)
            and candidate in steady)

  # A sentence first, being the one worth reading back; then a single word.
  for pattern, sentence, extract in ((r"\A[\w.,! ]+\Z", True, lines), (r"\A\w{2,}\Z", False, words)):
    only = extract(true_raw) - extract(false_raw)
    for candidate in sorted((_.strip() for _ in only if _.strip()), key=len):
      if not re.match(pattern, candidate):
        continue
      if sentence and not (settings.SINGLE_WHITESPACE in candidate and len(candidate) > settings.CANDIDATE_SENTENCE_MIN_LENGTH):
        continue
      if usable(candidate, true_raw, false_raw, changed_true, true_steady):
        return "--string=" + quoted_value(candidate)

  for candidate in sorted((_.strip() for _ in words(false_raw) - words(true_raw) if _.strip()), key=len):
    if re.match(r"\A\w+\Z", candidate) and usable(candidate, false_raw, true_raw, changed_false, false_steady):
      return "--not-string=" + quoted_value(candidate)

  """
  Nothing the page says on its own tells the two apart, so the markup it says it in is tried.

  A page that lists its own source carries the words of both answers as text and differs only in
  which of them it rendered - so the tag around the difference is the difference, and quoting it is
  what makes the answer nameable at all.
  """
  for option, page, other, on_true, steady in (("--string", true_raw, false_raw, True, true_steady),
                                               ("--not-string", false_raw, true_raw, False, false_steady)):
    for _, i1, i2, j1, j2 in opcodes:
      found = unique_around(page, other, *((j1, j2) if on_true else (i1, i2)))
      # Held to what the answer changed here too, not to what the page moves on its own.
      if found and found.strip() in steady:
        return option + "=" + quoted_value(found)
  return ""

"""
The option that says which answer is which on this target, for the finding to be reported with.
"""
def boolean_oracle_hint(technique):
  if technique != settings.INJECTION_TECHNIQUE.BOOLEAN_BASED:
    return ""
  # Said only where the run worked it out for itself: a run that was already given one is being
  # told what it told us.
  if boolean_oracle_given():

def boolean_oracle(page, code=None, page_length=None, headers=None):

  a true answer from a false one is as often something the application set in a header - a cookie
  it drops, a location it redirects to, a length it reports - as anything it rendered, and a body
  read on its own never sees it. The pattern is matched the way that one matches it too, without
  regard to case and with '^' and '$' reading the lines of the answer rather than the whole of it.
  """
  answered = page or ""
  if headers:
    try:
      answered = "".join(str(line) for line in headers.headers) + answered
    except AttributeError:
      answered = str(headers) + answered
  if menu.options.string:
    return menu.options.string in answered
  if menu.options.not_string:
    return menu.options.not_string not in answered

  all ('--null-connection') - either way, a length and nothing else is what there is to bisect on.

    to_false = abs(page_length - settings.BOOLEAN_FALSE_LENGTH)

  settings.BOOLEAN_TRUE_LENGTH = settings.BOOLEAN_FALSE_LENGTH = None

    return False

  # settled once, off the page this run actually has, rather than assumed.

  its own that varies in width, a timing or a counter, is a different number of bytes long on two
  identical requests, and a difference read off that is the page moving rather than the question
  being answered: taken for an answer, any boundary at all is confirmed on the strength of it.

having to learn it. Where the two answers differ by a word that also appears elsewhere on the page,

  corner will all differ between two requests without saying anything about what was asked. Text is

  these to count - otherwise the page's own furniture can stand in for the answer and be offered as

  which of them it rendered - so the tag around the difference is the difference, and quoting it is
  what makes the answer nameable at all.

"""
Move a value already confirmed working (by another technique) to the front of a candidate list.
"""
def _prioritize(candidates, confirmed_value):
  if confirmed_value in candidates:
    return [confirmed_value] + [c for c in candidates if c != confirmed_value]
  return candidates

"""
Every (whitespace, prefix, suffix, separator) combination to try, in order.
"""
def _boundary_combinations(whitespaces, prefixes, suffixes, separators, keep_output=False, grammar_separators=None):
  """
  Each boundary worth sending, once.

  A prefix that is itself a separator is dropped where it meets one, which every separator does -
  so from the second level up, every one of them arrives at the payload as the empty prefix that
  was already tried. Raising the level then buys re-sending what has been sent rather than asking
  anything new: at level three that is most of the combinations, over every technique alike.

  The suffix goes the same way. Against a payload that already closed itself, a separator suffix
  reads as ';;' or '&|' - no shell parses either - and a quote suffix balances only its own prefix.
  """
  # What the grammar calls a separator, which is not the same as what this target can chain on -
  # a suffix is dead against a closed payload either way.
  grammar_separators = separators if grammar_separators is None else grammar_separators
  # Asked of the function that puts the terminator there, so the two cannot drift apart.
  self_terminated = dict((separator, checks.terminate_payload("x", separator, keep_output) != "x") for separator in separators)
  tried = set()
  for whitespace in whitespaces:
    for prefix in prefixes:
      for suffix in suffixes:
        for separator in separators:
          if suffix and self_terminated[separator] and suffix in grammar_separators:
            continue
          if suffix in settings.QUOTES and suffix != prefix:
            continue
          # The same rule the payload is built under, so what is compared is what would be sent.
          effective = "" if (prefix + separator) in settings.JUNK_COMBINATION else prefix
          boundary = (whitespace, effective, suffix, separator)
          if boundary in tried:
            continue
          tried.add(boundary)
          # Asked of every boundary rather than of the technique as a whole, which is the point of
          # the two options: '--technique' already chooses between techniques.
          if not checks.test_selected(whitespace, effective, suffix, separator):
            continue
          yield whitespace, prefix, suffix, separator

"""
Put the boundaries the parameter's own value asks for first.

A value written as a number is rarely quoted in the command it ends up in, and one written as a
word often is - so which of the two shapes is tried first is worth taking from the value rather
than from the order the lists happen to carry. Worked out once per shape, for every parameter that
has it.
"""
def _order_by_value_shape(prefixes, suffixes):
  # Read off the parameter's own value, which is what the shape is a fact about. Where the sink
  # turned out not to need that value it has been stood in for by three random letters, and three
  # letters of the alphabet are alphabetic every time - so reading the stand-in put the quoted
  # boundaries first on every target that optimisation fired on, leaving the bare one last behind
  # four pairs and every separator of each. The value it stands for is kept, and is read instead;
  # where it was not kept, nothing is known about the shape and the lists are left as written.
  value = (settings.TESTABLE_VALUE or "").strip()
  if settings.VALUE_SKIPPED_EARLY:
    value = (settings.VALUE_SKIPPED_EARLY[0] or "").strip()
  elif settings.TESTABLE_VALUE_OPTIMIZED:
    return prefixes, suffixes
  if checks.is_digit(value):
    quoted_last = True
  elif value.isalpha():
    quoted_last = False
  else:
    return prefixes, suffixes
  key = (quoted_last, tuple(prefixes), tuple(suffixes))
  if key not in settings.BOUNDARY_ORDER_CACHE:
    # Sorted rather than split, so that what is not being moved keeps the order it was written in.
    quoted = lambda candidate: any(quote in candidate for quote in settings.QUOTES)
    settings.BOUNDARY_ORDER_CACHE[key] = (
      sorted(prefixes, key=lambda candidate: quoted(candidate) == quoted_last),
      sorted(suffixes, key=lambda candidate: quoted(candidate) == quoted_last)
    )
  return settings.BOUNDARY_ORDER_CACHE[key]

"""
Put a boundary combo another technique already confirmed for this parameter first.
"""
def _prioritize_confirmed_boundary(prefixes, suffixes, separators, whitespaces):
  prefixes, suffixes = _order_by_value_shape(prefixes, suffixes)
  _boundary = settings.CONFIRMED_BOUNDARY.get(settings.CHECKING_PARAMETER)
  if _boundary:
    _b_prefix, _b_suffix, _b_separator, _b_whitespace = _boundary

    Settled for this parameter, not merely tried first.

    reads; the techniques after it are asked through that one rather than through one more ordering
    of the whole space, which is what the reference does once an injection has a boundary of its own.

    The separator is left to the sweep. It is not part of that answer here the way a prefix is: what
    chains at this sink is a question each technique settles for itself, and one that refuses an
    operator another proved - boolean-based will not take a bare '&' - still needs its own turn.

    prefixes = [_b_prefix] if _b_prefix in prefixes else _prioritize(prefixes, _b_prefix)
    suffixes = [_b_suffix] if _b_suffix in suffixes else _prioritize(suffixes, _b_suffix)
    separators = _prioritize(separators, _b_separator)

def _announce_technique(injection_type, technique):

  announced = (settings.CHECKING_PARAMETER, checks.technique_label(injection_type, technique))
  already_announced = settings.LAST_ANNOUNCED_TECHNIQUE == announced
  # A technique retried internally - the file-based search across writable-directory candidates,
  # most of all - would otherwise repeat the "Testing/Continue testing" line once per candidate.
  # Said once, the same way injection_process() already holds its own repeats back.
  if already_announced and settings.LAST_RESUMED_TECHNIQUE == announced:

  checks.testing_technique_title(injection_type, technique)

action rather than being read again when it finally runs.

def _deferred_action(action, time_related_attack=None):
  if time_related_attack is None:
    time_related_attack = settings.TIME_RELATED_ATTACK
  # The action itself, carrying the flag that was in force when it was held back.
  def run():
    settings.TIME_RELATED_ATTACK = time_related_attack

# Register a post-detection action, run once at quit().
def _register_post_detection_action(action, time_related_attack=None):
  settings.PENDING_POST_DETECTION_ACTIONS.append(_deferred_action(action, time_related_attack))

def _register_os_shell_entry(action, time_related_attack=None):
  settings.PENDING_OS_SHELL_ENTRY = _deferred_action(action, time_related_attack)

def exit_handler(no_result):
  if no_result:

      """
      Every combination tried without one is the technique finished, so it is closed the way a
      technique that found something closes: a parameter that answers nothing would otherwise
      leave each of its techniques hanging on the dots it got to.

      if settings.PROGRESS_LINE_OPEN:

        # rather than ending it: its line is left open for the boundaries the sweep returns to, so
        # the one technique is announced once and closed once, however many directories it took.
        if not settings.TEMPFILE_BASED_STATE:

"""
Move a value already confirmed working (by another technique) to the front of a candidate list.
"""
def _prioritize(candidates, confirmed_value):
  if confirmed_value in candidates:
    return [confirmed_value] + [c for c in candidates if c != confirmed_value]
  return candidates

"""
Every (whitespace, prefix, suffix, separator) combination to try, in order.
"""
def _boundary_combinations(whitespaces, prefixes, suffixes, separators, keep_output=False, grammar_separators=None):
  """
  Each boundary worth sending, once.

  A prefix that is itself a separator is dropped where it meets one, which every separator does -
  so from the second level up, every one of them arrives at the payload as the empty prefix that
  was already tried. Raising the level then buys re-sending what has been sent rather than asking
  anything new: at level three that is most of the combinations, over every technique alike.

  The suffix goes the same way. Against a payload that already closed itself, a separator suffix
  reads as ';;' or '&|' - no shell parses either - and a quote suffix balances only its own prefix.
  """
  # What the grammar calls a separator, which is not the same as what this target can chain on -
  # a suffix is dead against a closed payload either way.
  grammar_separators = separators if grammar_separators is None else grammar_separators
  # Asked of the function that puts the terminator there, so the two cannot drift apart.
  self_terminated = dict((separator, checks.terminate_payload("x", separator, keep_output) != "x") for separator in separators)
  tried = set()
  for whitespace in whitespaces:
    for prefix in prefixes:
      for suffix in suffixes:
        for separator in separators:
          if suffix and self_terminated[separator] and suffix in grammar_separators:
            continue
          if suffix in settings.QUOTES and suffix != prefix:
            continue
          # The same rule the payload is built under, so what is compared is what would be sent.
          effective = "" if (prefix + separator) in settings.JUNK_COMBINATION else prefix
          boundary = (whitespace, effective, suffix, separator)
          if boundary in tried:
            continue
          tried.add(boundary)
          # Asked of every boundary rather than of the technique as a whole, which is the point of
          # the two options: '--technique' already chooses between techniques.
          if not checks.test_selected(whitespace, effective, suffix, separator):
            continue
          yield whitespace, prefix, suffix, separator

"""
Put the boundaries the parameter's own value asks for first.

A value written as a number is rarely quoted in the command it ends up in, and one written as a
word often is - so which of the two shapes is tried first is worth taking from the value rather
than from the order the lists happen to carry. Worked out once per shape, for every parameter that
has it.
"""
def _order_by_value_shape(prefixes, suffixes):
  # Read off the parameter's own value, which is what the shape is a fact about. Where the sink
  # turned out not to need that value it has been stood in for by three random letters, and three
  # letters of the alphabet are alphabetic every time - so reading the stand-in put the quoted
  # boundaries first on every target that optimisation fired on, leaving the bare one last behind
  # four pairs and every separator of each. The value it stands for is kept, and is read instead;
  # where it was not kept, nothing is known about the shape and the lists are left as written.
  value = (settings.TESTABLE_VALUE or "").strip()
  if settings.VALUE_SKIPPED_EARLY:
    value = (settings.VALUE_SKIPPED_EARLY[0] or "").strip()
  elif settings.TESTABLE_VALUE_OPTIMIZED:
    return prefixes, suffixes
  if checks.is_digit(value):
    quoted_last = True
  elif value.isalpha():
    quoted_last = False
  else:
    return prefixes, suffixes
  key = (quoted_last, tuple(prefixes), tuple(suffixes))
  if key not in settings.BOUNDARY_ORDER_CACHE:
    # Sorted rather than split, so that what is not being moved keeps the order it was written in.
    quoted = lambda candidate: any(quote in candidate for quote in settings.QUOTES)
    settings.BOUNDARY_ORDER_CACHE[key] = (
      sorted(prefixes, key=lambda candidate: quoted(candidate) == quoted_last),
      sorted(suffixes, key=lambda candidate: quoted(candidate) == quoted_last)
    )
  return settings.BOUNDARY_ORDER_CACHE[key]

"""
Put a boundary combo another technique already confirmed for this parameter first.
"""
def _prioritize_confirmed_boundary(prefixes, suffixes, separators, whitespaces):
  prefixes, suffixes = _order_by_value_shape(prefixes, suffixes)
  _boundary = settings.CONFIRMED_BOUNDARY.get(settings.CHECKING_PARAMETER)
  if _boundary:
    _b_prefix, _b_suffix, _b_separator, _b_whitespace = _boundary
    """
    Settled for this parameter, not merely tried first.

    A technique that broke out of the string already answered which prefix and suffix this sink
    reads; the techniques after it are asked through that one rather than through one more ordering
    of the whole space, which is what the reference does once an injection has a boundary of its own.

    The separator is left to the sweep. It is not part of that answer here the way a prefix is: what
    chains at this sink is a question each technique settles for itself, and one that refuses an
    operator another proved - boolean-based will not take a bare '&' - still needs its own turn.

"""
Calculate the time related execution time
"""
_injection_lock = threading.Lock()
_injections_in_flight = 0
_transport_before_injection = None

# Send one payload, with the timeout widened to allow for the delay it asks for.
def perform_injection(prefix, suffix, whitespace, payload, vuln_parameter, http_request_method, url):
  global _injections_in_flight, _transport_before_injection
  # A time-related payload asks the target to sleep, so the answer is meant to be late. Waiting less
  # than the delay we asked for turns our own request into a connection error, which on a target
  # slow enough to need a raised delay would abort the scan.
  needed = injected_delay_allowance()
  """
  These two are read at the moment the socket is opened, and several workers can be here at once -
  so what is saved and put back is the state before the first of them arrived, not before each. Any
  other bookkeeping restores one worker's idea of the timeout while another's request is still in
  flight, and that request times out on a delay it correctly asked for.
  """
  with _injection_lock:
    if _injections_in_flight == 0:
      _transport_before_injection = (settings.TIMEOUT, settings.KEEP_ALIVE)
    _injections_in_flight += 1
    if needed > settings.TIMEOUT:
      settings.TIMEOUT = needed
      # A pooled connection keeps the timeout it was opened with, so a reused one would ignore this.
      settings.KEEP_ALIVE = False
  try:
    return _perform_injection(prefix, suffix, whitespace, payload, vuln_parameter, http_request_method, url)
  finally:
    with _injection_lock:
      _injections_in_flight -= 1
      if _injections_in_flight == 0 and _transport_before_injection is not None:
        settings.TIMEOUT, settings.KEEP_ALIVE = _transport_before_injection
        _transport_before_injection = None

"""
Seconds a request needs to allow for, when the payload deliberately delays the answer.
"""
def injected_delay_allowance():
  if not settings.TIME_RELATED_ATTACK:
    return 0
  delay = settings.CALIBRATED_TIMESEC or menu.options.timesec or 0
  # What the payload actually asks for, not what was configured - a target whose delay is built
  # differently would otherwise have its own answer cut off, which reads as no delay at all.
  # The false-positive round adds a few seconds of its own on top of the calibrated delay.
  return checks.injected_delay(delay) + settings.TIME_DELAY_STEP + 10

# How commix is put together

Written for somebody about to change something and wanting to know what they are standing on. It
follows a payload: where it is built, what it is wrapped in, how it leaves, what is made of the
answer, and what survives to the next target. The source settles anything this disagrees with.

## A payload's journey

A run is one loop around a target, and a target is one loop around its parameters.

`commix.py` checks the interpreter and hands over to `src/core/main.py`. `run()` settles what can be
settled before there is a target at all - `src/core/startup.py: bootstrap()` - and then finds the
targets: a URL, a request file, a proxy log, a bulk file, a crawl, a sitemap, standard input.

For each of them `main()` connects once and reads that answer for everything it can tell: the
character encoding, the web server, the technology behind it, the operating system. The page itself
is kept (`requests.capture_original_page()`), because what a parameter is later compared against,
what the forms are parsed out of and what the proof is written from all want the same page, and none
of them is worth a second request.

Then `controller.do_check()`, and from there the shape is:

    perform_checks()        which places are tested, and in what order
      injection_process()   one parameter: heuristics, then technique after technique
        do_injection()      a finding - report it, store it, go on to exploitation

`perform_checks()` walks the URL, the POST body, the cookies, the standard headers and any custom
header. How far down that list it gets is what `--level` decides.

## What is being injected into

Two different things, and the distinction runs through the whole tree.

**A shell.** The value is handed to a command. A payload is a command chained onto the original with
a separator, and what makes it work is the shell's syntax.

**An evaluator.** The value is evaluated as code in the application's own language (`--eval`). A
shell separator means nothing here - a semicolon is a semicolon in a PHP statement, not a chain. The
payload has to be valid code in the language doing the evaluating.

The techniques are the same for both, so the two sinks are two sets of payload builders behind one
set of handlers:

|  | shell | evaluator |
|--|-------|-----------|
| payloads | `src/core/techniques/<technique>/*_payloads.py` | `src/core/eval/payloads/<technique>.py` |
| where the syntax comes from | the target's shell | `src/core/eval/grammars/php.py`, `python.py` |

A grammar carries its own probe, the functions that run a command, the boundaries that break into an
evaluated string and close it again, and the print statement results come back through. Teaching
commix another language is a new module in `grammars/` and nothing else.

## The techniques

Each one is three modules with the same shape, and reading them in this order is the fastest way to
understand any of them:

    *_payloads.py   what gets sent
    *_injector.py   sending it and reading the answer
    *_handler.py    running the technique, and pulling output through it once it works

| Technique | Package | Asked for with | Where the answer is read |
|-----------|---------|----------------|--------------------------|
| results-based | `techniques/results_based/` | `--technique=r` | the page |
| dynamic code evaluation | `eval/` | `--eval=<language>` | the page |
| boolean-based | `techniques/boolean_based/` | `--technique=b` | which of two pages the answer resembles |
| time-based | `techniques/time_based/` | `--technique=t` | how long the answer took |
| file-based | `techniques/file_based/` | `--technique=f` | a file under the web root |
| tempfile-based | `techniques/tempfile_based/` | under `f`, where the web root cannot be written | a file in a temporary directory |
| out-of-band | `techniques/oob/` | `--oob` | a request the target makes to a server you control |

`AVAILABLE_TECHNIQUES` is `r`, `b`, `t`, `f` and nothing else. Out-of-band is kept out of it on
purpose: it is a switch, so that the modules can use it too, and those never go through
`--technique`. The evaluator composes with the four letters rather than replacing them -
`EVAL_TECHNIQUE_LETTER` is what it went by before `--eval` existed, kept so that stored sessions
still read, and `c` is what results-based was called before it was renamed.

Every blind technique retrieves a character at a time and bisects on its ordinal. The payload
therefore asks a yes/no question, and the technique's own channel - a delay, a file, a request made
elsewhere, the page itself - carries the yes. Only the boolean-based one pays nothing for asking,
which is also why it alone can overlap its requests: nothing is being measured, so `--threads`
speeds it up where it would corrupt a technique reading the clock.

## Building the payload

A command becomes a payload by being wrapped and carried.

**Boundaries.** `settings.PREFIXES`, `SUFFIXES` and `SEPARATORS`, narrowed to the level in force by
`apply_injection_level()`, which reads them off the `_LVL1/2/3` lists.
`handler.py: _boundary_combinations()` walks every combination worth sending and drops the ones that
collapse onto something already tried - a prefix that is itself a separator arrives as the empty
prefix that was tried first, and a suffix is dead against a payload that has already closed itself.

**Choosing among them.** `--test-filter` and `--test-skip`, through `checks.test_selected()`, asked
of every boundary rather than of the technique as a whole.

**Whitespace.** `settings.WHITESPACES`, which a tamper script is allowed to rewrite.

**Tampering.** One script per file in `src/tamper/`. A script defines `tamper(payload)` and hands it
back rewritten. Where a script needs the whole request instead of the payload, `xforwardedfor.py` is
the precedent, hooked in `headers.do_check()`. `checks.tamper_scripts()` loads them and
`perform_payload_modification()` applies them in order.

**Carriers.** Where the parameter's value arrived written in something - Base64, hex, whatever
`--param-encoding` names or detection worked out - the payload is written out the same way. A value
answered in a different encoding from the one it came in is not that parameter's value.

## Getting it there and back

`src/core/requests/`

Every request leaves through one door. `headers.check_http_traffic()` builds the opener, applies the
policy, sends, reads and logs. A caller that wants to read or time the answer itself goes through
`headers.send_raw()`, which still applies the policy and is still counted. `requests.py` is what the
rest of the code actually calls: `get_request_response()`, the per-technique request builders, the
page-stability check.

Two things to know before changing anything here, both learned the hard way:

- **`settings.TOTAL_OF_REQUESTS` is not just a tally.** `stability.should_keep_retrying()`,
  `expand_retry_budget()` and `request_was_retried()` all read it. Count a request without growing
  the budget beside it and the retry loop starves - after which every later request quietly falls

# How commix is put together

Written for somebody about to change something and wanting to know what they are standing on. It
follows a payload: where it is built, what it is wrapped in, how it leaves, what is made of the
answer, and what survives to the next target. The source settles anything this disagrees with.

## A payload's journey

A run is one loop around a target, and a target is one loop around its parameters.

`commix.py` checks the interpreter and hands over to `src/core/main.py`. `run()` settles what can be
settled before there is a target at all - `src/core/startup.py: bootstrap()` - and then finds the
targets: a URL, a request file, a proxy log, a bulk file, a crawl, a sitemap, standard input.

character encoding, the web server, the technology behind it, the operating system. The page itself
is kept (`requests.capture_original_page()`), because what a parameter is later compared against,
what the forms are parsed out of and what the proof is written from all want the same page, and none
of them is worth a second request.

Then `controller.do_check()`, and from there the shape is:

    perform_checks()        which places are tested, and in what order
      injection_process()   one parameter: heuristics, then technique after technique
        do_injection()      a finding - report it, store it, go on to exploitation

`perform_checks()` walks the URL, the POST body, the cookies, the standard headers and any custom
header. How far down that list it gets is what `--level` decides.

## What is being injected into

Two different things, and the distinction runs through the whole tree.

**A shell.** The value is handed to a command. A payload is a command chained onto the original with
a separator, and what makes it work is the shell's syntax.

**An evaluator.** The value is evaluated as code in the application's own language (`--eval`). A
shell separator means nothing here - a semicolon is a semicolon in a PHP statement, not a chain. The
payload has to be valid code in the language doing the evaluating.

The techniques are the same for both, so the two sinks are two sets of payload builders behind one
set of handlers:

|  | shell | evaluator |
|--|-------|-----------|
| payloads | `src/core/techniques/<technique>/*_payloads.py` | `src/core/eval/payloads/<technique>.py` |
| where the syntax comes from | the target's shell | `src/core/eval/grammars/php.py`, `python.py` |

A grammar carries its own probe, the functions that run a command, the boundaries that break into an
evaluated string and close it again, and the print statement results come back through. Teaching
commix another language is a new module in `grammars/` and nothing else.

Each one is three modules with the same shape, and reading them in this order is the fastest way to
understand any of them:

    *_payloads.py   what gets sent
    *_injector.py   sending it and reading the answer
    *_handler.py    running the technique, and pulling output through it once it works

| Technique | Package | Asked for with | Where the answer is read |
|-----------|---------|----------------|--------------------------|
| results-based | `techniques/results_based/` | `--technique=r` | the page |
| dynamic code evaluation | `eval/` | `--eval=<language>` | the page |
| boolean-based | `techniques/boolean_based/` | `--technique=b` | which of two pages the answer resembles |
| time-based | `techniques/time_based/` | `--technique=t` | how long the answer took |

"""
Keep the page the target answered with, off the response already in hand.

Read once and handed back for whatever reads it next: what a parameter is compared against, what the
forms are parsed out of, and what the proof is written from all want the same page, and none of them
is worth a second request.
"""
def capture_original_page(response):
  if response is None or isinstance(response, bool):
    return None
  try:
    raw_body = response.read()
  except Exception:
    return None
  response.read = (lambda _b: lambda *a, **kw: _b)(raw_body)
  settings.ORIGINAL_PAGE = checks.decode_page_body(raw_body, response)
  return raw_body

"""
Check if the content of the given URL is stable over time.
"""
def is_url_content_stable(url, response=None, fetch_time=None, http_request_method=None):
  status = "stable"
  info_msg = "Checking if the target URL content is stable."
  settings.print_data_to_stdout(settings.print_info_msg(info_msg))

  # One request for the stability check, built the way the run's own requests are.
  def _build_request():
    method = http_request_method or settings.HTTPMETHOD.GET
    if settings.USER_DEFINED_POST_DATA:
      request = _urllib.request.Request(url, settings.USER_DEFINED_POST_DATA.encode(settings.DEFAULT_CODEC), method=method)
    else:
      request = _urllib.request.Request(url, method=method)
    headers.do_check(request)
    return request

  # Retried here too: what differs between the samples is set aside as the page moving on its own.
  def _sample(request=None, response=None):
    if request is None:
      request = _build_request()

Let's think about exact detection algorithm that meaningfully reduces false positives.

Current heuristic sends two payload variants per whitespace (Unix, Windows) and regex matches marker sequence. The candidate output is expected number surrounded by marker pair. A reflection false positive matches because the entire payload string contains `marker1 + 3 + marker2`. A WAF may echo payload. A page could also contain random 6-letter markers by chance but unlikely due to expected number too.

Response-difference scoring should:
- Strip reflected payload from candidate page. If after stripping expected markers disappear, it's a reflection => score 0.
- Confirm candidate markers are new compared to baseline and control.
- Send a **control** payload with a different expected output (e.g. `expected + 1`) through same boundary. If candidate expected appears in control response, then the target is just printing parts of input or guessing; reject.
- Compare candidate vs baseline/control: if all responses identical after removing reflection, reject.

Time blind validation:
- When response score is strong, optionally confirm with a delay. But for a target that reflects payload, the probe might be reflected but not executed; if the server sleeps on `sleep` only when executed, timing confirms. However if reflection strips `$()`? Using raw `;sleep N;` might itself be reflected, no delay. Good.
- Need avoid adding request cost to every candidate if response score is strong. Could use score tiers: `score >= STRONG` direct acceptance (after retries), `score >= SUSPICIOUS` then timing verify. But user asks time blind validation, so at least run it when direct evidence isn't conclusive.

- Send each heuristic payload up to `settings.FALSE_POSITIVE_RETRIES` or `--retries` until a response, with exponential/backoff? `menu.options.retries`.
- Require repeated positive evidence: e.g. 2/3 hits. This reduces transient false positives. But true positive requires multiple requests. Existing heuristic already sends multiple payloads; extra cost acceptable.
- Could detect flakiness and use majority.

Integration test: OOB DNS data flow exercised end-to-end.

Spins up a local DNS UDP stub on a random high port, installs a fake
`nslookup` wrapper script that forwards queries to that stub, generates
dns_exfil_command shell pipelines from the production code, runs them
in a subprocess, then verifies that the captured labels reassemble back
to the original command output.

No root access required; no external network traffic.

import itertools

import queue
import shutil
import socket
import stat
import struct
import subprocess

import threading
import re

TOKEN   = "testtoken0000"           # 13 chars
HOSTNAME = CORR_ID + TOKEN + ".test.local"


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Minimal DNS UDP stub
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

class DnsStub:
    """
    Listens on a random local UDP port, records every DNS query name it
    receives, and sends a minimal NXDOMAIN reply so callers do not block.
    """

    def __init__(self):
        self._sock = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_DGRAM)
        self._sock.bind(("127.0.0.1", 0))
        self._sock.settimeout(0.3)
        self.port = self._sock.getsockname()[1]
        self._q = queue.Queue()
        self._running = False
        self._thread = None

    def start(self):
        self._running = True
        self._thread = threading.Thread(target=self._loop, daemon=True)
        self._thread.start()

    def stop(self):
        self._running = False
        try:
            self._sock.close()
        except OSError:
            pass
        if self._thread:
            self._thread.join(timeout=2)

    def _loop(self):
        while self._running:
            try:
                data, addr = self._sock.recvfrom(512)
            except (socket.timeout, OSError):
                continue
            name = self._parse_name(data)
            if name:
                self._q.put(name.lower())
            self._nxdomain(data, addr)

    def _nxdomain(self, query, addr):
        if len(query) < 12:
            return
        hdr = bytearray(query[:12])
        hdr[2] = 0x81   # QR=1, RD=1
        hdr[3] = 0x83   # RA=1, RCODE=3
        hdr[6] = hdr[7] = 0
        try:
            self._sock.sendto(bytes(hdr) + query[12:], addr)
        except OSError:
            pass

    @staticmethod
    def _parse_name(data):
        if len(data) < 13:
            return None
        pos = 12    # skip the 12-byte DNS header
        labels = []
        while pos < len(data):
            length = data[pos]
            if length == 0:
                break
            pos += 1
            if pos + length > len(data):
                return None
            labels.append(data[pos:pos + length].decode("ascii", errors="replace"))
            pos += length
        return ".".join(labels) if labels else None

    def drain(self, first_wait=5.0, idle=0.5):
        """Collect all query names: wait up to *first_wait* s for the first
        one, then keep draining until *idle* s of silence."""
        names = []
        try:
            names.append(self._q.get(timeout=first_wait))
        except queue.Empty:
            return names
        while True:
            try:
                names.append(self._q.get(timeout=idle))
            except queue.Empty:
                break
        return names

import socket, sys, struct

host = sys.argv[1]
labels = host.lower().encode("ascii", errors="replace").split(b".")
question = b"".join(bytes([len(l)]) + l for l in labels) + b"\\x00"
question += struct.pack("!HH", 1, 1)        # QTYPE=A, QCLASS=IN
header = struct.pack("!HHHHHH", 0xAABB, 0x0100, 1, 0, 0, 0)

s.settimeout(2)

except Exception:

_NSLOOKUP_SH = """\
#!/bin/sh

_NOOP_SH = "#!/bin/sh\nexit 1\n"


def _install_fake_nslookup(tmpdir, port):
    sender = os.path.join(tmpdir, "_dns_sender.py")
    wrapper = os.path.join(tmpdir, "nslookup")
    with open(sender, "w") as fh:

    with open(wrapper, "w") as fh:
        fh.write(_NSLOOKUP_SH.format(sender=sender))
    os.chmod(wrapper, stat.S_IRWXU | stat.S_IRGRP | stat.S_IXGRP)

def _hex(text):
    return binascii.hexlify(text.encode(settings.DEFAULT_CODEC)).decode()


class MockChannel:
    """Minimal OOB channel returning a fixed set of DNS interactions."""

    def __init__(self):
        self._interactions = {}  # token -> [Interaction]
        self._labels = {}        # id(interaction) -> [label, ...]
        self._np_counter = 0

    def add(self, token, index, total, hex_data):
        label0 = str(index) + "-" + (str(total) if total is not None else "")
        itr = Interaction(protocol="dns", identifier="dummy." + token, raw_request="")
        self._labels[id(itr)] = [label0] + hex_data if isinstance(hex_data, list) else [label0, hex_data]
        self._interactions.setdefault(token, []).append(itr)
        return itr

    def seen(self, token, protocol=None):
        hits = list(self._interactions.get(token, []))
        return [i for i in hits if i.protocol == protocol] if protocol else hits

    def data_of(self, interaction):
        return self._labels.get(id(interaction), [])

    def poll_now(self):
        pass

    def new_payload(self):
        self._np_counter += 1
        token = "t{:012d}".format(self._np_counter)
        return token, "corrid" + token + ".oast.fun"


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# decode_dns_output — pure reassembly from a chunks dict
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

class TestDecodeDnsOutput(unittest.TestCase):

    def test_single_chunk_ascii(self):
        self.assertEqual(payloads.decode_dns_output({1: _hex("hello")}), "hello")

    def test_multiple_chunks_in_order(self):
        hexed = _hex("hello world")
        mid = (len(hexed) // 2) & ~1  # keep even so no half-byte
        self.assertEqual(
            payloads.decode_dns_output({1: hexed[:mid], 2: hexed[mid:]}),
            "hello world",
        )

    def test_chunks_out_of_order_reassembled_correctly(self):
        hexed = _hex("abcdef")
        mid = (len(hexed) // 2) & ~1
        # deliver chunk 2 first
        self.assertEqual(
            payloads.decode_dns_output({2: hexed[mid:], 1: hexed[:mid]}),
            "abcdef",
        )

    def test_trailing_newline_stripped(self):
        self.assertEqual(payloads.decode_dns_output({1: _hex("hello\n")}), "hello")

    def test_trailing_crlf_stripped(self):
        self.assertEqual(payloads.decode_dns_output({1: _hex("hello\r\n")}), "hello")

    def test_empty_chunks_returns_empty_string(self):
        self.assertEqual(payloads.decode_dns_output({}), "")

    def test_non_ascii_bytes_round_trip(self):
        # od -tx1 encodes every byte, so non-ASCII survives the round trip.
        raw = b"\xc3\xa9l\xc3\xa8ve"  # UTF-8 "élève"
        hexed = binascii.hexlify(raw).decode()
        result = payloads.decode_dns_output({1: hexed})
        self.assertEqual(result.encode(settings.DEFAULT_CODEC, errors="replace"), raw)

    def test_gap_in_chunk_indices_returns_partial_decode(self):
        # decode_dns_output joins whatever chunks arrived in index order; a gap does not
        # crash it.  INCOMPLETE_OUTPUT is set by _dns_output after the loop, not here.
        hexed = _hex("abcdef")
        third = (len(hexed) // 3) & ~1
        # chunks 1 and 3 present; chunk 2 missing — result is defined but not "abcdef"
        result = payloads.decode_dns_output({1: hexed[:third], 3: hexed[third * 2:]})
        self.assertIsInstance(result, str)

    def test_contiguous_chunks_do_not_set_incomplete(self):
        hexed = _hex("hello world")
        mid = (len(hexed) // 2) & ~1
        settings.INCOMPLETE_OUTPUT = False
        payloads.decode_dns_output({1: hexed[:mid], 2: hexed[mid:]})
        self.assertFalse(settings.INCOMPLETE_OUTPUT)

    def test_hex_labels_are_lowercased_by_resolver(self):
        # A resolver may uppercase labels; decode_dns_output must still work.
        hexed = _hex("hi").upper()
        self.assertEqual(payloads.decode_dns_output({1: hexed}), "hi")


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# _dns_output — the chunk-collection loop that drives the mock channel
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

class TestDnsOutputLoop(unittest.TestCase):

    def setUp(self):
        settings.OOB_TIMEOUT = 15
        settings.INCOMPLETE_OUTPUT = False

    # --- loop-format (separator `;`/`\n`): label carries "index-total" ---

    def test_loop_format_single_chunk(self):
        token = "aaa"
        ch = MockChannel()
        ch.add(token, index=1, total=1, hex_data=_hex("hello"))
        # time: call 1 → deadline base (0), call 2 → inside loop, never reached because
        # total is known and len(chunks)>=total breaks before the deadline check.
        with mock.patch("time.time", side_effect=[0, 0]):
            with mock.patch("time.sleep"):
                result = oob_injector._dns_output(ch, token)
        self.assertEqual(result, "hello")

    def test_loop_format_multi_chunk_all_arrive(self):
        token = "bbb"
        hexed = _hex("hello world")
        mid = (len(hexed) // 2) & ~1
        ch = MockChannel()
        ch.add(token, index=1, total=2, hex_data=hexed[:mid])
        ch.add(token, index=2, total=2, hex_data=hexed[mid:])
        with mock.patch("time.time", side_effect=[0, 0]):
            with mock.patch("time.sleep"):
                result = oob_injector._dns_output(ch, token)
        self.assertEqual(result, "hello world")

    def test_loop_format_out_of_order_arrival(self):
        # Chunks registered in reverse order; index key must still sort correctly.
        token = "ccc"
        hexed = _hex("xyz123")
        mid = (len(hexed) // 2) & ~1
        ch = MockChannel()
        ch.add(token, index=2, total=2, hex_data=hexed[mid:])
        ch.add(token, index=1, total=2, hex_data=hexed[:mid])
        with mock.patch("time.time", side_effect=[0, 0]):
            with mock.patch("time.sleep"):
                result = oob_injector._dns_output(ch, token)
        self.assertEqual(result, "xyz123")

    # --- xargs-format (separator `&`/`|`): label carries "index-" (no total) ---
    # quiet_polls reaches 2 after two iterations with no new chunks → break.

    def test_xargs_format_exits_on_quiet_polls(self):
        token = "ddd"
        ch = MockChannel()
        ch.add(token, index=1, total=None, hex_data=_hex("world"))

class DnsStub:
    """
    Listens on a random local UDP port, records every DNS query name it
    receives, and sends a minimal NXDOMAIN reply so callers do not block.
    """

    def __init__(self):
        self._sock = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_DGRAM)
        self._sock.bind(("127.0.0.1", 0))
        self._sock.settimeout(0.3)
        self.port = self._sock.getsockname()[1]
        self._q = queue.Queue()

        self._thread = None

    def start(self):
        self._running = True
        self._thread = threading.Thread(target=self._loop, daemon=True)
        self._thread.start()

    def stop(self):
        self._running = False
        try:
            self._sock.close()
        except OSError:
            pass
        if self._thread:
            self._thread.join(timeout=2)

    def _loop(self):
        while self._running:
            try:
                data, addr = self._sock.recvfrom(512)
            except (socket.timeout, OSError):
                continue
            name = self._parse_name(data)
            if name:

    def _nxdomain(self, query, addr):

        hdr[3] = 0x83   # RA=1, RCODE=3
        hdr[6] = hdr[7] = 0

            self._sock.sendto(bytes(hdr) + query[12:], addr)
        except OSError:

        if len(data) < 13:
            return None
        pos = 12    # skip the 12-byte DNS header
        labels = []

            if length == 0:

            pos += 1
            if pos + length > len(data):
                return None
            labels.append(data[pos:pos + length].decode("ascii", errors="replace"))
            pos += length
        return ".".join(labels) if labels else None

        """Collect all query names: wait up to *first_wait* s for the first
        one, then keep draining until *idle* s of silence."""
        names = []

            except queue.Empty:

+#!/usr/bin/env python
+# encoding: UTF-8
+
+"""
+This file is part of Commix Project (https://commixproject.com).
+Copyright (c) 2014-2026 Anastasios Stasinopoulos (@ancst).
+
+This program is free software: you can redistribute it and/or modify
+it under the terms of the GNU General Public License as published by
+the Free Software Foundation, either version 3 of the License, or
+(at your option) any later version.
+
+For more see the file 'readme/COPYING' for copying permission.
+"""
+
+import difflib
+
+from src.utils import settings
+
+"""
+Evidence read off a response, rather than off one regular expression.
+
+The heuristic's markers are random, but a page can still carry them for a reason that is not the
+command: the parameter is reflected, a filter quotes the payload back, or the page happens to move
+between the two requests. A score puts those readings together, so that a marker found only in the
+answer the command was asked for, and only after the payload itself was taken out, is worth more
+than a page that merely changed.
+"""
+class ResponseEvidence(object):
+  def __init__(self, score, marker_hits, marker_total, baseline_similarity,
+               control_similarity, strong, reason):
+    self.score = score
+    self.marker_hits = marker_hits
+    self.marker_total = marker_total
+    self.baseline_similarity = baseline_similarity
+    self.control_similarity = control_similarity
+    self.strong = strong
+    self.reason = reason
+
+  def __repr__(self):
+    return ("ResponseEvidence(score=" + str(round(self.score, 1)) +
+            ", markers=" + str(len(self.marker_hits)) + "/" + str(self.marker_total) +
+            ", reason='" + str(self.reason) + "')")
+
+"""
+A pair of timing answers, and whether the delayed one stands clear of the ordinary one often
+enough to be believed.
+"""
+class TimeBlindEvidence(object):
+  def __init__(self, confirmed, hits, attempts, control_times, delayed_times, margin, reason):
+    self.confirmed = confirmed
+    self.hits = hits
+    self.attempts = attempts
+    self.control_times = control_times
+    self.delayed_times = delayed_times
+    self.margin = margin
+    self.reason = reason
+
+  def __repr__(self):
+    return ("TimeBlindEvidence(confirmed=" + str(self.confirmed) +
+            ", hits=" + str(self.hits) + "/" + str(self.attempts) +
+            ", reason='" + str(self.reason) + "')")
+
+def _text(page):
+  return page if isinstance(page, str) else ""
+
+"""
+How alike two pages are, from 0 to 1.
+
+The same sequence matcher the rest of the run compares pages with, kept here without importing the
+controller back into itself. Pages too large to read character by character fall back to their
+lengths, which is still enough to notice that one is not the other.
+"""
+def page_similarity(first, second):
+  first, second = _text(first), _text(second)
+  if first == second:
+    return 1.0
+  if not first or not second:
+    return 0.0
+  if max(len(first), len(second)) > getattr(settings, "MAX_COMPARISON_LENGTH", 1000000):
+    ratio = 1.0 * len(first) / len(second)
+    return ratio if ratio <= 1 else 1.0 / ratio
+  try:
+    return difflib.SequenceMatcher(None, first, second).quick_ratio()
+  except (MemoryError, TypeError, ValueError):
+    return 0.0
+
+"""
+Score how much of an answer is evidence rather than page noise, from 0 to 100.
+
+'markers' are the strings that only a command's output should carry - normally the random marker
+pair around the computed value. A marker already on the baseline page, or on the control answer,
+is not this answer's evidence. 'control' is the same question asked with a value that cannot be
+the command's output; a candidate that reads like that control is the request being echoed, not
+the command being run.
+"""
+def score_response_difference(baseline, candidate, control=None, markers=None,
+                              threshold=None):
+  threshold = settings.DETECTION_SCORE_THRESHOLD if threshold is None else threshold
+  baseline, candidate = _text(baseline), _text(candidate)
+  control = None if control is None else _text(control)
+  markers = [str(marker) for marker in (markers or []) if marker]
+
+  if not candidate:
+    return ResponseEvidence(0.0, [], len(markers), 0.0, 0.0, False, "empty answer")
+
+  baseline_similarity = page_similarity(baseline, candidate)
+  control_similarity = page_similarity(control, candidate) if control is not None else None
+  changed = max(0.0, 1.0 - baseline_similarity)
+  control_changed = max(0.0, 1.0 - control_similarity) if control is not None else changed
+
+  marker_hits = []
+  for marker in markers:
+    if marker not in candidate:
+      continue
+    if marker in baseline:
+      continue
+    if control is not None and marker in control:
+      continue
+    marker_hits.append(marker)
+
+  if markers:
+    marker_score = 100.0 * len(marker_hits) / len(markers)
+  else:
+    marker_score = 0.0
+
+  """
+  Once the payload itself has been taken back out, a real result is usually a small number of
+  characters added to a page that is otherwise unchanged - so a marker carries most of the weight,
+  and the page difference and the control only decide whether that marker is believable.
+  """
+  if marker_hits:
+    score = (0.70 * marker_score +
+             0.15 * min(100.0, changed * 100.0) +
+             0.15 * min(100.0, control_changed * 100.0))
+  else:
+    score = (0.50 * min(100.0, changed * 100.0) +
+             0.50 * min(100.0, control_changed * 100.0))
+
+  reason = "marker evidence"
+  if control is not None and candidate == control and candidate != baseline:
+    score = min(score, 10.0)
+    reason = "answer matches the control"
+  elif not marker_hits and not changed:
+    score = 0.0
+    reason = "answer matches the baseline"
+  elif not marker_hits:
+    reason = "response difference without a marker"
+
+  return ResponseEvidence(score, marker_hits, len(markers), baseline_similarity,
+                          control_similarity, score >= threshold, reason)
+
+"""
+The number only, for callers that do not need the reasons behind it.
+"""
+def response_difference_score(baseline, candidate, control=None, markers=None,
+                              threshold=None):
+  return score_response_difference(baseline, candidate, control, markers, threshold).score
+
+"""
+Call something again while it has no usable answer, up to a bounded number of attempts.
+
+'accept' is asked of every result; without one, anything other than None/False is accepted. The
+last result is handed back where the budget runs out, so the caller still sees what the target
+last said rather than an invented failure.
+"""
+def retry_call(call, attempts=None, accept=None):
+  attempts = max(1, int(attempts if attempts is not None else settings.FALSE_POSITIVE_RETRIES))
+  last = None
+  for attempt in range(attempts):
+    try:
+      last = call(attempt)
+    except (KeyboardInterrupt, SystemExit):
+      raise
+    except Exception:
+      last = None
+    if accept is not None:
+      if accept(last):
+        return last
+    elif last is not None and last is not False:
+      return last
+  return last
+
+def _elapsed(value):
+  if isinstance(value, (tuple, list)):
+    value = value[0] if value else None
+  try:
+    return float(value)
+  except (TypeError, ValueError):
+    return None
+
+"""
+Confirm that the target runs a command by timing one that waits and one that does not.
+
+The two are asked as a pair, so what is compared is this target's own pace at this moment rather
+than a delay against zero. A request that failed is retried, and one pair that is late enough is
+not enough on its own: a delayed answer has to clear the ordinary one by the configured share of
+the delay that was asked for, on enough of the paired attempts to be a pattern.
+
+The callbacks return either elapsed seconds or a tuple whose first item is elapsed seconds.
+"""
+def verify_time_based_blind(send_control, send_delayed, delay, attempts=None):
+  delay = float(delay)
+  attempts = max(1, int(attempts if attempts is not None else settings.FALSE_POSITIVE_RETRIES))
+  ratio = getattr(settings, "DETECTION_TIME_BLIND_RATIO", 0.6)
+  margin = max(getattr(settings, "MIN_VALID_DELAYED_RESPONSE", 0.5), delay * ratio)
+  control_times, delayed_times = [], []
+  usable_pairs = 0
+  hits = 0
+  reason = "not enough paired answers"
+
+  for attempt in range(attempts):
+    try:
+      control = _elapsed(send_control())
+      delayed = _elapsed(send_delayed())
+    except (KeyboardInterrupt, SystemExit):
+      raise
+    except Exception:
+      control = delayed = None
+    if control is None or delayed is None:
+      reason = "a paired answer was not retrieved"
+      continue
+    control_times.append(control)
+    delayed_times.append(delayed)
+    usable_pairs += 1
+    if delayed - control >= margin:
+      hits += 1
+      reason = "delayed answer cleared the ordinary one"
+    else:
+      reason = "delayed and ordinary answers were too close"
+
+  if not usable_pairs:
+    return TimeBlindEvidence(False, 0, attempts, control_times, delayed_times, margin, reason)
+
+  required = max(1, min(getattr(settings, "DETECTION_TIME_BLIND_HITS", 2), usable_pairs))
+  confirmed = hits >= required
+  if confirmed:
+    reason = "delay reproduced on " + str(hits) + "/" + str(usable_pairs) + " paired answers"
+  return TimeBlindEvidence(confirmed, hits, usable_pairs, control_times, delayed_times,
+                           margin, reason)
+

def command_injection_heuristic_basic(url, http_request_method, check_parameter, place):
  check_parameter = check_parameter.lstrip().rstrip()
  checks.perform_payload_modification(payload="")
  basic_payload_generator()
  if menu.options.interpreter:
    basic_payloads = settings.ALTER_INTERPRETER_BASIC_COMMAND_INJECTION_PAYLOADS
  else:
    basic_payloads = settings.BASIC_COMMAND_INJECTION_PAYLOADS

  basic_payloads = [x.replace(settings.RANDOM_STRING_GENERATOR, settings.SINGLE_WHITESPACE.strip()) for x in basic_payloads]

  """
  One shape per shell, and only the shape worth sending.

  The two payloads are the same question asked in each shell's own syntax, so which of them answers
  is what names the shell. Where the operating system is already known - the banner said so, or
  '--os' did - the other shape cannot execute, and sending it only doubles the requests.
  """
  shaped = list(zip(basic_payloads, ("Unix-like", "Windows")))
  if settings.IDENTIFIED_TARGET_OS or menu.options.os:
    wanted = "Windows" if settings.TARGET_OS == settings.OS.WINDOWS else "Unix-like"
    shaped = [pair for pair in shaped if pair[1] == wanted] or shaped

  settings.RESULTS_BASED_STATE = True
  try:
    for whitespace in settings.WHITESPACES:
      if not settings.IDENTIFIED_COMMAND_INJECTION:
        for payload, shell_os in shaped:
          response, url = heuristic_request(url, http_request_method, check_parameter, payload, whitespace, place)
          if type(response) is not bool and response is not None:
            html_data = checks.process_page_content(response, action="decode")
            match = re.search(settings.BASIC_COMMAND_INJECTION_RESULT, html_data)
            if match:
              settings.IDENTIFIED_COMMAND_INJECTION = True
              checks.note_printer_that_answered(html_data)
              # Asked while the payload that answered is still in hand, and before a technique has
              # spent a single request at the slow value's price.
              url = probe_skip_testable_value_early(url, http_request_method, check_parameter, payload, whitespace, place)
              # The token the rest of the code compares against, and then what was really shown.
              checks.set_target_os(shell_os)
              # A payload that ran answers what the banner could not, so nothing need be asked.
              settings.OS_IDENTIFICATION_PENDING = False
              announce_heuristic_finding("identified command shell type: '" + checks.target_shell_label() + "'")
              # A shell answering here says nothing about whether a string is also evaluated as
              # code, so it settles the question only where the code injection sink was not asked
              # for by name - otherwise every technique carrying it would skip itself, and the run
              # would report "not injectable" without having sent one of their payloads.
              if not menu.options.eval_sink:
                settings.SKIP_CODE_INJECTIONS = True
              elif not settings.COMMAND_SUGGESTED:
                settings.COMMAND_SUGGESTED = True
                """
                '--eval' names code injection, and naming it is what stops command injection from
                being tested at all - so a shell answering here would otherwise be found, reported
                and then left behind, with the run going on to look only for what it was told to.

                The option the user gave still wins by default: what is offered is dropping it,
                and a run that is not being watched keeps the option it was started with.
                """
                message = "The target answers as a command shell, so it is open to command injection as well. "
                message += "Do you want to test for that instead (i.e. without the '--eval' option)? [y/N] "
                if common.read_input(message, default="N", check_batch=True) in settings.CHOICE_YES:
                  menu.options.eval_sink = False
                  settings.SKIP_CODE_INJECTIONS = True
              break

    settings.RESULTS_BASED_STATE = False
    return url

  except (_urllib.error.URLError, _urllib.error.HTTPError) as err_msg:
    settings.print_data_to_stdout(settings.print_critical_msg(err_msg))
    raise SystemExit(settings.EXIT_FAILURE)

"""
Build a raw shell numeric comparison for false-positive checks; Unix-only.
"""
def condition_check(separator, condition, timesec, http_request_method):
  if settings.TARGET_OS == settings.OS.WINDOWS:
    return None
  if settings.SKIP_SUBST and separator in (";", "\n", "\r\n", "&"):
    """
    An 'if'/'then'/'fi' block branches on a real exit status using nothing but 'test' and a
    statement terminator - where '[ condition ]' followed by reading '$?' needs a ']' and a '$',
    both of which a filter that blocks command substitution outright is just as likely to block
    too. ';', '\n' and '\r\n' all terminate a statement on their own, so the separator under test
    is what glues 'if' to 'then' to 'fi' for those three - nothing else belongs in a payload built
    to prove that one of them, specifically, is what chains commands here. '&' backgrounds rather
    than terminates, and cannot glue the block together itself; a newline is the one thing every
    one of 'then' and 'fi' needs regardless, so it is the fallback for that case alone.

+The marker pair is part of the payload, so a page that echoes the request contains it as surely as
+a page where the command ran does. Removing the reflected payload first leaves the marker only
+where the target itself wrote it.

  settings.TESTABLE_VALUE_STOOD_IN_FOR = original_value
  settings.VALUE_SKIPPED_EARLY = (original_value, placeholder, original_url, original_data)

  # and a stand-in this run goes on to refuse would be left for the next one to replay.
